title: Signed integer-shift identity for double-Hom cochain evaluation
statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative ring and let $P,J,I$ be arbitrary integer-indexed cochain complexes of $R$-modules, that is, of module sheaves on the one-object site with trivial topology and constant ring $R$ [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules]. Use shifts $U[m]^n=U^{n+m}$ with differential $(-1)^m d_U$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], product Hom $\operatorname{Hom}^\bullet$ with $d(f)=d_{\rm target}f-(-1)^{|f|}fd_{\rm source}$ [def-pur-hom-complex], and direct-sum total tensor [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. Put $A=\operatorname{Hom}^\bullet(J,I)$ and $\mathcal G(P)=\operatorname{Hom}^\bullet(\operatorname{Hom}^\bullet(P,J),I)$. Denote by $E_P:A\otimes_RP\to\mathcal G(P)$ the chain evaluation $E_P(h\otimes x)(f)=(-1)^{|x||f|}h(f(x))$.
For any complexes $U,V$ and integer $m$, let $s^V_{U,m}:\operatorname{Hom}^\bullet(U[m],V)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Hom}^\bullet(U,V)[-m]$ be the chain isomorphism given on degree-$q$ maps by source reindexing and the factor $(-1)^{mq}$. Then the natural chain isomorphisms
$$\chi_{P,m}=(-1)^m s^I_{\operatorname{Hom}^\bullet(P,J),-m}\circ\operatorname{Hom}^\bullet(s^J_{P,m},I)^{-1}:\mathcal G(P[m])\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal G(P)[m],$$
$$\tau_{P,m}:A\otimes_RP[m]\xrightarrow{\sim}(A\otimes_RP)[m],\qquad h\otimes x\longmapsto(-1)^{m|h|}h\otimes x$$
satisfy, for every integer $m$, the equality of chain maps
$$\chi_{P,m}\circ E_{P[m]}=E_P[m]\circ\tau_{P,m}.$$
More explicitly, for $g\in\mathcal G(P[m])^n$ and $f\in\operatorname{Hom}^\bullet(P,J)^c$, one has $(\chi_{P,m}g)(f)=(-1)^{m(n+c)}g(f)$, where on the right $f$ is reindexed to degree $c+m$ in $\operatorname{Hom}^\bullet(P[m],J)$. No K-flatness, K-injectivity or boundedness is required.

proof.text: Work on the one-object site, so the complexes and maps of [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules] are ordinary complexes and linear maps of $R$-modules. By [def-pur-hom-complex] and [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves], the formula for $E_P$ defines a degree-zero linear map: for $|h|=a$, $|x|=b$, $|f|=c$, its value lies in $I^{a+b+c}$. It is balanced in $h,x$, linear in the entire homogeneous family $f$, and extends over the direct sum because each input is a finite sum of homogeneous tensors. Thus no infinite sum is used, even when all complexes are unbounded.

proof.text:
Check the chain condition using the two differential definitions [def-pur-hom-complex, def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. For homogeneous $h,x,f$ of degrees $a,b,c$, expanding $(dE_P(h\otimes x))(f)$ gives
$$(-1)^{bc}d_Ih(f(x))-(-1)^{a+bc}h(d_Jf(x))+(-1)^{a+bc+c}h(f(d_Px)).$$
Expanding $E_P(d_Ah\otimes x+(-1)^a h\otimes d_Px)(f)$ gives these same three terms, since $d_Ah=d_Ih-(-1)^ahd_J$ and $(b+1)c=bc+c$. Equality on all homogeneous $f$ is equality of product-Hom elements, and equality on homogeneous tensors extends by linearity. The same calculation applies with $P[m]$ in place of $P$.

source.place: Tags 0A60 (lemma-evaluate-and-more), 0A61 (remark-sign-explanation), and section-sign-rules; explicit agent calculation in the stated normalization.

proof.text:
Verify the first-variable shift without importing any choice of shift normalization. For a degree-$q$ family $f:U[m]\to V$, reindex it as a degree-$(q-m)$ family $U\to V$. With the shift differential of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] iterated to integer $m$, both $s_{U,m}^V(df)$ and $d(s_{U,m}^Vf)$, after reindexing, are
$$(-1)^{mq+m}d_Vf-(-1)^{mq+q}fd_U.$$
This follows by substituting $d_{U[m]}=(-1)^md_U$ in the Hom differential [def-pur-hom-complex]. The inverse reindexes back and multiplies a degree-$q$ element on the shifted Hom side by the same $(-1)^{mq}$; its square sign is $1$. Degree-zero pre- and postcomposition commute with these signs, proving naturality in $U,V$.

proof.text:
For $h\in A^a$ and $x\in P^b$, regard $x$ as degree $b-m$ in $P[m]$. The map $\tau$ is degree zero and has inverse given by the same sign $(-1)^{ma}$. Using [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves] and the shift convention [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], both $\tau d(h\otimes x)$ and $d\tau(h\otimes x)$ are
$$(-1)^{ma+m}d_Ah\otimes x+(-1)^{ma+a+m}h\otimes d_Px.$$
It is therefore a chain isomorphism. Its formula commutes with degree-zero maps of $A,P$, so it is natural.

proof.text: Put $B=\operatorname{Hom}^\bullet(P,J)$ and $B_m=\operatorname{Hom}^\bullet(P[m],J)$. By step 3, $s=s^J_{P,m}:B_m\to B[-m]$ is a natural chain isomorphism. Contravariant composition in [def-pur-hom-complex] sends its inverse to the inverse of $\operatorname{Hom}^\bullet(s,I)$, so the displayed composite defining $\chi$ is a natural chain isomorphism. Explicitly, for $g\in\mathcal G(P[m])^n$ and $f\in B^c$, applying $s^{-1}$ to $f$ in $B[-m]^{c+m}$ contributes $(-1)^{m(c+m)}$. The outer $s^I_{B,-m}$ contributes $(-1)^{-mn}$, and the prefactor contributes $(-1)^m$. Their product is $(-1)^{m(n+c)}$, since $m^2+m$ is even. This proves exactly the asserted component formula, for positive, zero and negative $m$.

source.place: Tags 0A60 (lemma-evaluate-and-more), 0A61 (remark-sign-explanation), and section-sign-rules; explicit agent calculation in the stated normalization.

proof.text:
Finally take $|h|=a$, $|x|=b$ in the original $P$, and $|f|=c$ in $B$. In the shifted source $|x|=b-m$, $f$ is read in $B_m^{c+m}$, and $E_{P[m]}(h\otimes x)$ has degree $n=a+b-m$. By step 5, the left side of the claimed square evaluates on $f$ to $h(f(x))$ times the sign with exponent
$$(b-m)(c+m)+m(a+b-m+c).$$
The right side has exponent $ma+bc$, by $\tau$ and the formula for $E_P$. Their difference is $2m(b-m)$, which is even for every integer $m$. Hence the two values agree. Product-Hom equality is componentwise [def-pur-hom-complex], and homogeneous tensors generate the direct-sum total tensor [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves], so this proves equality of the chain maps. Every construction and check used only linear maps and signs, with no flatness, injectivity or boundedness assumption.
